author: Max Greve
title: For some time now, I have been keeping readers updated on th
text:
For some time now, I have been keeping readers updated on the progress of Amazon ( AMZN ) in the tablet market in relation to the other major tablet players, including Alphabet’s ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ) Android devices and Microsoft ( MSFT ) as well as Apple ( AAPL ) iPad, the tablet king.
Until now I have paid relatively little attention to the impact of Amazon’s new Fire strategy on the last two members of the top five, Lenovo ( OTCPK:LNVGY ) and Huawei. However, there is more new data available about the tablet market. It appears Amazon is now preparing the next step in its device strategy, with particular implications for those companies. Lenovo will be the focus of this article.
A Shifting Market I have written about Amazon Fire at length, and I won’t rehash everything here. In my view, Amazon’s tablet performance has greater implications than some believe because of the gateway it provides to Amazon Prime, the company’s drug of choice for inducing binge-purchasing across its entire inventory of physical goods on its website.
At first, it appeared to me that Amazon’s determination to put Fire back on the map posed the biggest threat to the other tech giants trying to dominate the tablet space. Apple’s iPad saw a sales decline persist for several years, while Microsoft has never really managed to break through strongly to begin with. Android, of which Amazon Fire is a skinned derivative, also has struggled lately. 
Meanwhile Amazon has rebounded to become the third-largest seller of tablets globally, despite only offering Fire in the US and a few other countries, while its competitors are generally available worldwide. It competes for this No. 3 spot with Huawei, while Apple, Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) and Lenovo are firmly ensconced above and below them.
Market Data Analysis I will be using IDC data again, which has released its third quarter tablet market figures but not yet its holiday numbers. At first glance, they’re just more of the same. As I observed last quarter Apple and Amazon are both advancing deeper and deeper into the market, reversing earlier stalls in sales and growing market share. Meanwhile Samsung and Google’s Android tablets more broadly are still showing slow but steady declines, as is Microsoft’s Surface line.
A few points, however. First, Amazon set a new third quarter company best to record faster growth in its tablet segment than Apple. Not only in percentage terms but also in absolute numbers, where Amazon beat Apple by 30%, 1.3 million to 1 million. Meanwhile Lenovo and Huawei also recorded continued growth. Of the top five tablet makers, only Samsung showed a decline.
Second, IDC observed that most of the growth it is seeing is in lower-cost tablets - even Apple recently released a cheaper iPad - and that also bodes well for Amazon, which has made low-cost tablets the center of its tablet strategy. It also bodes well, or would seem to, for Lenovo and Huawei. Samsung and Microsoft are the big losers from a shift down market. 
Third, this explosive growth came before the unveiling of Amazon’s newest device, Fire HD 10, which has received strong reviews and offers consumers a true full-sized tablet viewing experience. The boost from that device isn’t even reflected here, but should make itself felt this quarter and going forward. Unlike Amazon, Lenovo and Huawei don’t have a comparable boost coming here - their lines are rather mature and not expected to produce a comparable category expansion or move upmarket.
Fourth, Amazon appears to remain far better able than any other company to monetize its tablets after the point of sale, with a combination of Prime subscriptions, digital content sales, and shopping physical goods on Amazon’s website.
Amazon Ready To Expand? These points would all seem to suggest that the international expansion of Fire is a question of when, not if, and that there isn’t much groundwork left to lay. Amazon’s tablet effort has until now been geographically constrained. This made sense as it tried to recover from a rather catastrophic strategy shift toward higher-priced products and restore momentum to its product line. 
But sales are now growing strongly again, and a big enough base has been created to support software and app development by third parties. And Amazon is sending signals that it thinks it’s ready to go truly global with its device line. Amazon brought Echo to India a month ago and is now preparing to bring Prime Music close on its heels. It already brought Fire TV to India last year. Fire tablets would be a very logical next step. Amazon also has begun selling Fire tablets in Canada.
Is Lenovo Especially Vulnerable? Amazon’s geographic expansion would not be good news for anyone, but it would hit Lenovo especially hard. 
As I noted in my last article, I have somewhat waned in my belief that Amazon will enter into a knock-down fight with Apple for tablet market share. Rather, it appears each will dominate its own end of the price spectrum in tablets. 
Samsung sells at all price points and would probably take a further hit from Amazon’s global expansion, but its primary competitor must be considered Apple, which lives at the high end where Samsung makes most of its revenue and practically all of its profit. Much the same goes for Microsoft.
That leaves Lenovo, Huawei, and various other smaller Android manufacturers who, like Amazon, live at the low end of the price range. While Lenovo and Huawei both achieved unit sales growth in the third quarter, they did so in the absence of a Fire tablet challenger, and with their key markets in Latin America and Asia largely unaffected by Amazon’s return to form in tablets. That may not be the case for much longer.
Lenovo's Last Growing Product Line Lenovo offers a diversified product mix, and to be sure not all its eggs are in the tablet basket. However, of its five key product categories - tablets, phones, servers, PCs, and cloud - phones and servers both reported negative operating income last quarter, and cloud is still in its early stages. 
That leaves tablets and PCs as Lenovo’s real cash generators. IDC reported that tablets were still growing, albeit too slowly for Lenovo’s tastes I’m sure, while PC sales were flat Y/Y. In other words, Lenovo has one growing product segment right now. And Amazon is about to challenge it. Amazon’s growth last quarter came to almost 60% of Lenovo’s total tablet sales. It grew four times as fast as Lenovo despite a more limited geographic footprint.
Lenovo did report a steady profit last quarter, so Amazon’s challenge will not push it into the red necessarily. But the threat of losing its only growing, profitable segment still should not be dismissed in my opinion. 
Investment Summary Amazon seems poised to expand its tablet line in the near future. While no one will be completely unaffected, except perhaps Apple, the threat to Lenovo seems particularly acute, and to a lesser extent Huawei. Meanwhile the failure of any Android vendor to compete with Amazon Fire also is a negative for Alphabet.
Amazon itself, meanwhile, should see further boosts to Prime membership from expanding Echo and Fire globally, much as it has in the US. That in turn should boost sales of physical retail items, accelerating Amazon's International sales growth.
While none of these companies swim or sink solely based on their tablet divisions, the potential for Amazon to take considerable market share still bears watching.
